title: ChinaTravel: An Open-Ended Benchmark for Language Agents in Chinese Travel Planning

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative and quantitative comparison of the new ChinaTravel benchmark against existing benchmarks (TravelPlanner) to demonstrate the latter's U.S.-centric focus and lack of diversity in travel scenarios (e.g., intercity vs. single-city trips).

Statistical analysis of constraint distributions (e.g., Zipf's law) and co-occurrence patterns to quantify the tendency of LLMs to generate simplistic and repetitive queries compared to diverse human-authored queries.

Designing a new metric, Conditional Logical Pass Rate (C-LPR), to address potential biases in existing metrics (Final Pass Rate) where agents might receive credit for satisfying logical constraints while violating fundamental environmental feasibility.
